scheme_name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Minor Irrigation
description:
The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank scheme for minor irrigation is a significant initiative by the Government of India aimed at enhancing agricultural productivity and promoting rural development.

This scheme was launched in 1978 as part of the broader strategy to support agricultural development in rural areas.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance for minor irrigation projects.

The government aims to increase the area under irrigation by supporting farmers in accessing necessary resources.

The scheme specifically targets small and marginal farmers who often lack access to adequate irrigation facilities.

The measurable target of the scheme is to enhance irrigation coverage by at least 10 percent in the areas where the scheme is implemented.

The scheme also aims to improve the income levels of farmers by increasing agricultural productivity through better irrigation facilities.

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided for various minor irrigation projects such as tube wells, bore wells, and surface irrigation systems.

The assistance provided can cover up to 50 percent of the total project cost for small and marginal farmers.

For example, if the total cost of a minor irrigation project is INR 1 lakh, the government can provide up to INR 50,000 as financial assistance.

The scheme also encourages the use of modern irrigation techniques to optimize water usage and enhance crop yields.

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on small and marginal farmers.

Small farmers are defined as those who own less than 2 hectares of land.

Marginal farmers are those who own less than 1 hectare of land.

The income criteria for eligibility are set at a maximum annual income of INR 2 lakh.

Farmers must also be members of a registered cooperative society to qualify for the benefits under this scheme.

The application process involves several steps to ensure transparency and accountability.

Farmers must first approach their local cooperative bank or society to express their interest in the scheme.

They will need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the cooperative bank.

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, landholding details, and the type of irrigation project proposed.

Farmers must also submit documents such as proof of land ownership, income certificate, and membership certificate of the cooperative society.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the bank's officials.

The bank will conduct a feasibility study of the proposed project to assess its viability.

If approved, the bank will disburse the financial assistance directly to the farmer's account.

The disbursement is typically done in two installments.

The first installment is released after the project is approved.

The second installment is released after the completion of the project and verification by the bank officials.

The timeline for the entire process can vary but typically takes around 3 to 6 months from application submission to fund disbursement.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development plays a crucial role in providing financial support and guidance.

State governments also have a significant role in implementing the scheme at the local level.

Farmers can contact their local cooperative bank for more information and assistance regarding the application process.

The scheme has been instrumental in improving irrigation facilities in rural areas.

It has contributed to increased agricultural productivity and income for many farmers.

Statistics indicate that the scheme has led to a significant increase in the area under irrigation in various states.

For instance, states like Punjab and Haryana have reported a 15 percent increase in irrigated land due to this scheme.

The scheme also promotes sustainable agricultural practices by encouraging the use of efficient irrigation methods.

Farmers are trained on the importance of water conservation and efficient irrigation techniques.

The government regularly conducts workshops and training sessions to educate farmers about the benefits of minor irrigation.

The scheme is aligned with the broader goals of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana.

This national initiative aims to ensure the availability of water to all agricultural fields in a planned and sustainable manner.

The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank scheme complements this by focusing on minor irrigation projects.

The success of this scheme is evident from the increased crop yields reported by farmers who have benefited from it.

Farmers have reported an increase in crop yields by up to 30 percent after the implementation of minor irrigation projects.

This increase in productivity has a direct positive impact on the livelihoods of farmers and their families.

The scheme also plays a crucial role in reducing the dependence on rain-fed agriculture.

By providing reliable irrigation facilities, farmers can cultivate multiple crops throughout the year.

This diversification of crops leads to improved food security in rural areas.

The scheme has also contributed to rural employment generation.

With the increase in agricultural activities, more job opportunities are created in rural areas.

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the impact of the scheme to ensure its effectiveness.

Feedback from farmers is regularly collected to make necessary adjustments to the scheme.

The scheme has undergone several revisions to improve its implementation and outreach.

In recent years, the government has introduced digital platforms to streamline the application process.

Farmers can now apply online for financial assistance under this scheme.

This digital initiative has made the process more accessible and transparent.

The government is committed to further enhancing the scheme to meet the evolving needs of farmers.

In conclusion, the Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank scheme for minor irrigation is a vital initiative for promoting agricultural development in India.

It provides essential financial support to small and marginal farmers.

The scheme aims to improve irrigation facilities and increase agricultural productivity.

With specific eligibility criteria and a structured application process, it ensures that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.

The ongoing support from the government and implementing agencies is crucial for the success of this scheme.
